Instead, multiple chromatic differences coexist, forming a complex manifold. The saturation gradient isomorphism reveals that even without a true ground-color, contrast emerges from differential saturation profiles—this invalidates Helmholtz’s static model. Fixation introduces a temporal decay kernel, implying that contrast perception is not invariant but evolves under sustained gaze. These primitives form a coherent framework for modeling visual inference: contrast field duality provides the static structure, saturation gradient isomorphism offers dynamic variation, and fixation decay kernel governs temporal evolution. Together, they define a non-linear, time-dependent visual state-space.
